transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm just really struggling with how my face looks, especially my skin. I have these horrible, ugly scars and acne all over my face, and it's causing me so much anxiety lately. I feel like it's all people see when they look at me.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time doing things like checking your skin in the mirror, trying to hide or cover it up, or asking others for reassurance?

Yes, I do. I constantly check my skin in the mirror throughout the day and spend hours trying to cover it up with heavy makeup and hats before I can even leave the house. I also find myself repeatedly asking my family if my skin looks okay, but I can never really believe them when they say it's fine.
Besides your concerns about your skin, do you find yourself constantly worrying about a variety of other everyday things, like your health, finances, work, or family?
No, I don't really worry about things like my health, finances, or family. Almost all of my anxiety and focus is completely consumed by my skin and how terrible it looks.
Do you experience any other repetitive thoughts or behaviors that aren't related to your appearance, such as a need to wash your hands repeatedly, check locks, or arrange things in a specific order?
No, I don't have any habits like washing my hands repeatedly or checking locks. All of my repetitive behaviors and worries are strictly focused on my appearance and trying to fix my skin.
How has this concern about your skin impacted your daily life, such as your work, social activities, or relationships?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about how it impacts my work or relationships because I'm just so focused on my skin all the time.
Have family members, friends, or doctors ever told you that your skin looks fine, or that the scars and acne you are concerned about are barely noticeable to them?

Yes, my family and even a dermatologist have told me my skin looks fine and that they can't see any scars. It's incredibly frustrating because to me, these flaws are so huge, ugly, and impossible to ignore. I feel like they are just saying that to make me feel better, but I know how awful it really looks.

latest_inference.note: The patient presents with a severe preoccupation with perceived flaws in their skin (scars and acne) that are unnoticeable to others, including a dermatologist. This preoccupation is accompanied by repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, reassurance seeking, and spending hours applying makeup to cover it up), causing significant distress. Generalized Anxiety Disorder and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder have been ruled out as the anxiety and repetitive behaviors are strictly focused on physical appearance. The presentation meets all DSM-5 criteria for Body Dysmorphic Disorder.
